decisions.reason: It extends the firm's established dumper and site-equipment knowledge, so with its own R&D and a growing market the firm is likely to learn quickly and refine rather than withdraw it.

As an articulated construction dumper close to the existing offer, it fits the firm's engineering, service and customer-adaptation capabilities and is therefore unlikely to be taken off the market soon.

Because the underground mine rescue vehicle is described as distant from the firm's established offer, absorptive-capacity limits make early learning and commercialization harder even though the firm has in-house R&D.
The compact telescopic loader builds on familiar machinery competences and customer channels, so management would usually keep it on the market and improve it through continued development.
